Proposed next steps:  
- If PO preferred: Laura Bennett (cc'd) from our finance team will provide vendor setup steps and required docs; Marcus will prepare a SOW that includes procurement language.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if that helps accelerate.

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Procurement policy: We typically require a PO for any vendor spend > $10k annually. Small purchases (< $10k) sometimes go through our procurement card.
- Vendor onboarding: Yes — our AP team requires a completed vendor form and a W9 for US vendors. Procurement will kick off portal setup (procurement@finact.com).
- Marketplace: If you have a listing on CloudMarket (or similar), buying there is faster, but billing is handled by the marketplace and we will not be able to get a Redwood invoice. That can complicate our internal chargeback process.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a PO + invoice flow? Also what net terms you offer (net-30, net-45)? Finally — please send the W9 and your standard vendor form if possible.

I’ll loop in procurement so they can advise on portal steps. Our target is to lock the procurement path by Friday so we can begin a pilot in April.

Best,

Hi Dana — jumping in to provide a quick runbook on the marketplace vs direct PO options so procurement can weigh the trade-offs:  

- Marketplace purchase (card):
  * Pros: Instant provisioning, simpler procurement for small pilots, typically faster start.
  * Cons: Billing routed through the marketplace operator; Redwood cannot attach a Redwood invoice or credit memos to that transaction. Marketplace may not support net terms.

- Direct PO / Invoice (Redwood invoice):
  * Pros: Standard enterprise billing, Redwood can issue invoices and support net-30 after credit approval; PO workflow supported.
  * Cons: Requires vendor onboarding (W9 + vendor form) and signed SOW before billing. May add ~5 business days for vendor setup depending on your AP backlog.

Links and attachments:  
- Marketplace listing (read-only): https://marketplace.example.com/redwood-inference
- Attached: vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (fields we typically see your AP ask for) and the SOW draft Jordan shared.

If procurement prefers PO, Laura (cc) can take the lead on required docs and next steps. Happy to sync on a quick call with procurement to answer technical questions about scoped usage and expected monthly spend (so they can route to the right approval band).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Hi Dana — Laura from Redwood finance here. Thanks for the context. To make the PO route smooth, please note the following mandatory items for our AP team before we can accept an invoice tied to a PO:  

1) Completed vendor onboarding form (we have a short portal; I can share a link).
2) A current W9 (for US vendors).
3) Signed agreement or SOW that references the PO number.
4) For net terms (net-30), we require internal credit approval — that typically takes 2–3 business days once vendor setup is complete.

If FinAct purchases via a marketplace, Redwood cannot generate a direct invoice to FinAct — billing will come from the marketplace operator and will appear on the marketplace statement. If your chargeback system requires a Redwood invoice line item, marketplace purchase may not satisfy that need.  

Next steps from Redwood finance:  
- I can send our vendor onboarding link and a sample vendor form (we accept e-submissions).
- Once you confirm PO preference and provide the PO number, we will route the SOW for signature and attach the PO to the SOW so invoicing is straightforward.

DocuSign link (sample): https://docusign.example.com/r/abcd-1234
Vendor form (sample): https://redwoodinference.example.com/vendor-setup

Please let us know what procurement prefers and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks,
